## What you are really learning

Use exact arithmetic, counting and string structure instead of fragile ad-hoc tricks.

The goal is not to learn 11 unrelated definitions. Compare the operations needed by each classic problem and notice which invariant survives from one technique to the next.

## Begin with a small example

Choosing two people from five is not a permutation.

$$
\binom{n}{k}=\frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}
$$

**What the symbols mean:** n is the number of distinct choices, k selected size, and factorial multiplies positive integers down to one.

**Substitute actual numbers:** With n=5 and k=2, compute 5!/(2!3!)=120/(2×6)=10 unordered pairs. Ordering those same pairs would overcount them.

This is how the topic pages below should be read: understand the numbers first, then generalise to the equation.

## The chapters in this family

1. **[Math](../math/index.qmd)** — Turn a computational task into equations, inequalities or discrete structures.
2. **[Number Theory](../number-theory/index.qmd)** — Reason about divisibility, modular arithmetic, primes, and gcd.
3. **[Combinatorics](../combinatorics/index.qmd)** — Count discrete arrangements, selections, and structures.
4. **[Probability and Statistics](../probability-and-statistics/index.qmd)** — Analyse uncertainty and infer quantities from samples.
5. **[Geometry](../geometry/index.qmd)** — Use coordinates, distances, orientation, and spatial relationships.
6. **[Bit Manipulation](../bit-manipulation/index.qmd)** — Use bitwise operators to encode and transform integer state.
7. **[Hash Function](../hash-function/index.qmd)** — Map objects into compact signatures or storage buckets.
8. **[Rolling Hash](../rolling-hash/index.qmd)** — Update a substring fingerprint using a fixed base and modulus.
9. **[String Matching](../string-matching/index.qmd)** — Find occurrences of a pattern inside a longer text.
10. **[Suffix Array](../suffix-array/index.qmd)** — Sort all suffix starting positions lexicographically for text queries.
11. **[Counting](../counting/index.qmd)** — Turn logical predicates into occurrence counts or frequency aggregates.

## Practice method

Choose ONE chapter. Reproduce its example with paper and pencil, identify what is cached or discarded, implement the tiny idea, and explain one case in which the algorithm's assumptions fail. Repeat until the invariant feels natural.

The [original executable examples](../examples/README.md) provide code you can run and test. If two topics seem similar, compare them in the [algorithm selection guide](../guides/choose-a-pattern.qmd).
